title: The Hand
question: Which wrist bone is glowing?
lines: One tiny wrist bone is named for a boat. Which one?
Watch the glowing bone on the thumb side of the wrist.
The lunate sits beside it, closer to the middle of the wrist.
This boat-shaped bone sits on the thumb side, next to the radius.
Why it matters: it's the wrist bone people break most often.

title: The Hand
question: How many bones are glowing?
lines: Your wrist is a puzzle of small bones. How many pieces?
Watch the group of bones between the hand and the forearm.
How many bones are in the glowing group?
Five bones form the palm, but those sit further down.
The wrist has two rows of four small bones, the carpals.
Why it matters: many small joints let your wrist bend and twist.
